text: Git branching is a core feature of version control that helps teams manage changes smoothly. Instead of working directly on the main code, developers create feature branches, which are separate copies of the project where they can experiment safely. Once a new feature is finished, the next step is merging, which brings those changes back into the main branch. However, before merging, you usually open a pull request. A pull request is a formal way to review and discuss the code with teammates before it gets combined. Overall, a clear branching workflow keeps projects organized, reduces conflicts, and makes collaboration faster and less stressful.
